---
name: dithercn
description: Build any dithered visual with the dithercn engine (dither-core, in lib/dither) in a React or shadcn app. Use when the user wants a dither, a dithered or Bayer or halftone or pixel texture, or a dithered background, hero, chart, meter, card, loader, text or image for a landing page or dashboard, or when code imports lib/dither or components/dithercn.
---

# dithercn

dithercn is a dither engine. `dither-core` (installed into `lib/dither`) turns a tone you compute into ordered dither dots, in your theme's colours, with motion, resizing and reduced motion handled. You build the dither the user asked for on top of it. The dithercn components are examples of what the engine can do, not a menu to pick from. Install one only when it is exactly what the user asked for. Otherwise write your own, and borrow technique from the closest example's source.

## 1. Set up the engine

Find the engine: `lib/dither/index.ts`, under the `lib` alias in `components.json` (imports below use `@/lib/dither`; use the project's alias). If it is missing, install it from the dithercn registry:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add https://dithercn.dev/r/dither-core.json
```

If it exists, check that it is current: `grep -q colorField lib/dither/shader.tsx` (with the project's path). An engine installed before `colorField` existed lacks it and the `spectrum` and `paletteColor` helpers, and TypeScript reports `Property 'colorField' does not exist`. Replace the engine's files; this keeps the project's `lib/utils.ts` (`yes n` answers no to every question about overwriting a file) and restores `lib/dither/export.ts`:

```bash
rm -rf lib/dither && yes n | npx shadcn@latest add https://dithercn.dev/r/dither-core.json https://dithercn.dev/r/dither-export.json
```

Don't use `--overwrite`: it also replaces `lib/utils.ts`. If the project edited files inside `lib/dither`, tell the user before replacing them.

That also installs `dither-tokens`: the CSS variables `--dither-ink`, `--dither-paper`, `--dither-cell`, `--dither-bloom` and `--dither-color-<name>`, written into the project's global CSS and mapped to the shadcn `--primary` and `--background`. The engine needs React 19 and Tailwind CSS v4.

Done when `lib/dither/index.ts` exists, `lib/dither/shader.tsx` mentions `colorField`, and the global CSS defines `--dither-ink`.

## 2. Pick the technique

| The user wants                                                                                                                        | Use                                                                           | Read                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| A surface whose tone varies per pixel or moves: gradients, glows, noise, contours, waves, rings, any shape you can describe with math | `DitherShader` with a GLSL `field`                                            | [fields.md](references/fields.md)                      |
| A static fill inside SVG shapes: bars, arcs, gauges, meters, rings, icons, maps                                                       | `FillPattern` or `DitherPattern` in `<defs>`, `fill="url(#id)"`               | [engine-api.md](references/engine-api.md#static-fills) |
| A static fill on a DOM element: a block, band, border, progress bar, skeleton                                                         | `fillStyle(variant)` or `ditherMaskStyle(level)` on an empty layer            | [engine-api.md](references/engine-api.md#static-fills) |
| Many hues at once: a rainbow, a spectrum, RGB, a different colour per line or shape                                                   | `DitherShader` with a `field` for the shape and a `colorField` for the colour | [fields.md](references/fields.md#colour)               |
| A photo or logo, dithered                                                                                                             | `ditherImage` on canvas pixels                                                | [engine-api.md](references/engine-api.md#images)       |
| A PNG, SVG or CSS file, or a background with no JavaScript                                                                            | `dither-export`                                                               | [engine-api.md](references/engine-api.md#export)       |

Combine them freely: a dashboard card can hold an SVG meter with `FillPattern` over a `DitherShader` glow.

The examples in [examples.md](references/examples.md) (written when the skill is installed; if it's missing, read https://dithercn.dev/.well-known/agent-skills/dithercn/references/examples.md) are references. If the user asked for exactly one of them, install it. If not, write your own: read the closest example's source for its field or SVG, then build the design the user described. Never swap the request for an example that is merely nearby, and never guess at an example's props; read its docs page or source.

Done when every visual in the request has a technique.

## 3. Build it

If the dither is for a landing page, or a section of one, read [landing-pages.md](references/landing-pages.md) before anything else. A good dither on a generic page still looks generated: the page has to be about the product, and the dither has to come from it.

1. Read the reference named for your technique, and [recipes.md](references/recipes.md) for complete, working components to adapt.
2. Write the component in its own file. `"use client"` when it uses `DitherShader`, hooks or a canvas; `FillPattern`, `DitherPattern`, `fillStyle` and `ditherMaskStyle` render on the server.
3. Give it typed props for what the user would tweak (colour, intensity, speed, scale, value), with defaults that already look good.
4. Place it with [placement.md](references/placement.md): a shader fills a positioned parent (`absolute inset-0`), and content sits in a sibling above it.
5. Colour it with [theme.md](references/theme.md): palette names such as `"ink"` and `"blue"`, or CSS variables, so it follows light and dark.

Done when the component renders the requested look with no `[dither-core]` errors in the console.

## 4. Check it in a browser

Open the page and look at it. Screenshot it if you can, at desktop and phone widths, in light and dark mode, and once with reduced motion (`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`). Hold it to [quality.md](references/quality.md).

Done when every check in quality.md passes. A screenshot that shows flat colour, a solid block or an empty box means the field returns the wrong range or the parent has no size: fix it and look again.

## Rules for every dither

- A field returns a continuous tone in [0, 1]: 0 paper, 1 ink. The engine quantises and dithers it, so write smooth math (`smoothstep`, `exp`, `mix`) and leave thresholds and Bayer matrices to the engine.
- `uv` runs 0 to 1 on both axes with y up. Multiply x by `res.x / res.y` before measuring distances, or circles stretch into ovals.
- Paint with theme colours (`"ink"`, palette names, `--css-variables`). Literal colours, and `spectrum()` in a `colorField`, are for when the user asks for specific colours or a rainbow.
- Text sits on clear ground. Fade the tone down where text goes: to 0 for lines and sparse patterns, to 0.2 or less for soft fills. Text contrast stays at 4.5:1 or better.
- Motion is slow, a drift of a few percent of the box per second. Choose `stillTime` so the reduced-motion frame looks finished.

# dither-core API Everything imports from `@/lib/dither` (the project's `lib` alias), except export functions, which live in `@/lib/dither/export`. The installed source in `lib/dither/` is the final word; each export has a doc comment. ## Shared types ```ts type DitherColor = DitherColorName | string; // A palette name ("ink" | "blue" | "purple" | "green" | "pink" | "orange" | "red" | "grey"), // a CSS variable name ("--chart-1"), or any CSS colour ("var(--chart-1)", "oklch(0.7 0.15 272)", "#fff", "transparent"). // Names win over CSS keywords: "red" is the dithercn red. type DitherPalette = readonly [DitherColor, DitherColor, ...DitherColor[]]; // From tone 0 (paper) to tone 1 (ink). At least two. type DitherMatrix = "bayer2" | "bayer4" | "bayer8" | "blue-noise"; ``` Matrices: `bayer4` is the default, a regular printed crosshatch with 17 tones. `bayer8` has 65 tones and finer gradients. `bayer2` is chunky, 5 tones. `blue-noise` is a 64×64 tile with no visible grid, like film grain; best for large soft surfaces. `level` (static fills) and tone (shaders) both mean coverage from 0 (no cells inked) to 1 (all). With `bayer4`, `k / 16` inks exactly k of every 16 cells. ## DitherShader A client component that draws a GLSL field as a dither on a WebGL canvas at one canvas pixel per cell, scaled up with crisp edges. ```tsx } className="absolute inset-0" // plus any div prop: style, ref, id, data-* /> ``` - The root is `relative overflow-hidden pointer-events-none`, `aria-hidden` by default. It renders no children: put content in a sibling. - It sizes to its box. A box with no height draws nothing. - `fallback` shows before the first frame, without WebGL, and while the shader is far offscreen. Default: flat `palette[0]`. Make it resemble the dither (a CSS gradient in the ink colour). - Free behaviour: resize observer, whole-device-pixel cells, theme changes re-read the palette, pauses offscreen and in hidden tabs, a still frame under reduced motion, context loss recovery. At most 8 shaders hold a WebGL context at once (`MAX_LIVE_CONTEXTS`); past that, a shader coming on screen takes one from a shader just off screen, never from one still on screen, and waits otherwise, showing `fallback`. - `data-state` on the root: `running`, `paused` (offscreen or hidden tab), `static` (reduced motion or `animate={false}`), `fallback` (no frame drawn). - With `colorField`, each cell is either paper (`palette[0]`) or the colour `colorField` returns there; the field's tone still decides which, so density and colour are independent. The rest of the palette is what the `paletteColor(x)` helper reads. Without it, the palette maps tone to colour as before. - Changing `uniforms`, `palette`, `matrix`, `levels` or `speed` is cheap. Changing the `field` or `colorField` string recompiles, so keep it a module constant and drive variation through uniforms. - `DitherShaderProps` is exported. A wrapper component usually takes `Omit` plus its own props, and spreads the rest. ## Static fills All server-safe and free after first paint. ### FillPattern (SVG) ```tsx ``` | Prop | Type | Default | Notes | | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `id` | `string` | required | Use `useId()` so two instances never collide. | | `fill` | `"gradient" \| "dotted" \| "hatched" \| "solid"` | required | `dotted`: a sparse lattice. `hatched`: diagonal lines. | | `color` | `DitherColor` | `"ink"` | | | `cell` | `number` | `3` | In SVG user units. With a scaling `viewBox` the cells scale too. | | `level` | `number` | `1` | Gradient only: coverage at the dense edge, or the even coverage without `ramp`. | | `floor` | `number` | `0.0625` | Gradient: coverage past the fade. | | `matrix` | `DitherMatrix` | `"bayer4"` | Gradient only. | | `ramp` | `{ edge: "top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right"; at: number; length: number; extent?: number }` | none | Gradient: densest at `edge`, located at coordinate `at`, fading over `length` user units. | `dotted` and `hatched` have a fixed coverage (a quarter of the cells); vary their strength with `opacity` or the colour. `fill="gradient"` without `ramp` fills one even `level`, like `DitherPattern`. `DitherPattern` is the older, simpler pattern: `` fills one even `level`, with an optional `background` colour behind the ink. Prefer `FillPattern` unless you need `background`. For exact pixel cells inside an SVG, give it a `viewBox` in CSS pixels that matches its rendered size (measure with a `ResizeObserver`), or keep the SVG at a fixed pixel size. ### fillStyle and ditherMaskStyle (DOM) ```tsx
``` - `fillStyle(variant, { color?, cell?, edge?, length?, from?, to?, matrix? })` returns a background colour plus a tiled CSS mask. Gradient: dense at `edge` (default `"bottom"`), fading over `length` cells (default 24) from coverage `from` (1) to `to` (0.0625). `cell` is CSS px or any CSS length; default `var(--dither-cell)`. - `ditherMaskStyle(level, { matrix?, cell? })` masks an element to one even coverage. Pair it with a background colour (`bg-dither-ink`, `bg-dither-blue`). - Both mask the element's children too, so apply them to an empty layer and put content in a sibling. - To animate density, cross-fade two layers with `opacity`. The mask itself does not transition. - Lower level: `ditherMask(level, { matrix?, cell? })` returns a CSS `url()` for `mask-image`; `ditherPath(level, matrix?)` the SVG path of one tile; `ditherRamp({ edge, length, extent?, from, to, matrix? })` a ramp tile. ### Bloom A soft glow in the fill's colour, `"off" | "low" | "high"`. `--dither-bloom` scales it per theme. - `…` wraps DOM content in a drop-shadow glow that follows the dithered cells. - `{solid copies of shapes}` is an SVG group drawn as a blurred glow; render it before the patterned shapes. - `bloomStyle(color, bloom)` returns `{ filter }` for any element. ## Colours - `cssColor(color: DitherColor): string`: `"green"` → `var(--dither-color-green, )`, `"--x"` → `var(--x)`, others unchanged. Use it for every inline colour. - `DITHER_COLOR_NAMES`, `SERIES_COLORS` (distinct hues in order, for multi-series data), `seriesColor(color, index)`. - `useDitherColors(ref, names?)`: resolves colours to `[r, g, b, a]` in [0, 1] and re-resolves on theme change; `null` before mount. Default names `["--dither-ink", "--dither-paper"]`. - `resolveColor(color, el?)`: one-off resolution in the browser. - Tailwind utilities from the tokens: `bg-dither-ink`, `text-dither-paper`, `bg-dither-blue`, `text-dither-green` and so on. ## Motion - `useFrameLoop((time, delta) => { … }, { target?: ref, enabled?: true, fps?: 30, stillTime?: 0 })`: a rAF loop that runs only while `target` is on screen and the tab is visible. Under reduced motion or `enabled: false` it calls once with `(stillTime, 0)`. Returns `"running" | "paused" | "static"`. Use it for canvas or DOM animation you write yourself. - `usePrefersReducedMotion()`, `useInView(ref, { rootMargin? })`, `useDocumentVisible()`. - `MOTION`: `{ ease: "cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)", fast: 150, base: 240, slow: 600 }` (ms) for CSS transitions. ## Images ```ts const out = ditherImage(context.getImageData(0, 0, w, h), { method: "atkinson", // "bayer4" | "bayer8" | "blue-noise" | "floyd-steinberg" | "atkinson" | "sierra-lite" palette: [ [0.04, 0.04, 0.06], [0.55, 0.62, 1], ], // RGB in [0, 1], nearest colour wins threshold: 0.5, }); context.putImageData(out, 0, 0); ``` Returns a new `ImageData`; the input is untouched. Draw the image at one pixel per cell (scale it down first), dither, then show the canvas scaled up with `image-rendering: pixelated`. Get theme colours for the palette from `useDitherColors`. Error-diffusion methods move dots everywhere when the input changes, so use them for still images and ordered methods for anything animated. Over about 512×512, run it in a Web Worker. ## Export `import { toPNG, toSVG, toCSS, download, svgDataUrl } from "@/lib/dither/export"`. The skill installs it; if `lib/dither/export.ts` is missing, run `npx shadcn@latest add https://dithercn.dev/r/dither-export.json`. - `toPNG(source: HTMLCanvasElement | PixelBuffer, { scale? }): Promise`: crisp upscale by a whole number. Browser only. - `toSVG(source: PixelBuffer | { width, height, indices }, { cell?, palette?, background? }): string`: merged runs, pure string. - `toCSS({ level, matrix?, cell?, ink?, paper?, mode?: "background" | "mask", selector? })`: one CSS rule that tiles a dither, no JavaScript at runtime. `mode: "mask"` paints with `ink` and accepts CSS variables; `"background"` bakes a literal ink colour into the tile. - `toCSS({ kind: "image", image, format?: "png" | "svg", selector? })`: a whole dither as a covering background. - `download({ data, filename, type? })` saves a Blob or string. To export what a `DitherShader` shows, compute the same tones on the CPU into a `PixelBuffer` and run `ditherImage` with an ordered method: the shader's WebGL canvas does not keep its pixels after drawing.

# Examples

Components built on the engine. They are references, not a menu: install one when it is exactly what the user asked for, and otherwise write your own and borrow technique from the closest one. Each installs as plain source into `components/dithercn/<name>.tsx`, so you can read its field or SVG. Install one with:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add https://dithercn.dev/r/<name>.json
```

Each docs page (the `.md` link) has usage, every prop and in-context examples. Read the installed source for the field and the technique.

## Backgrounds

- `aurora`: Curtains of light that fold, sway and shimmer, drawn as a dither, with props for colours, curtains, rays, tilt, drift and masks. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/aurora.md
- `beams`: God rays from a point or an edge that sweep slowly and fade with distance. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/beams.md
- `black-hole`: A black hole with a thin photon ring and a hot accretion disk seen at a slant, its far side lensed over the top and under the bottom, streaming round with one side brighter. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/black-hole.md
- `contours`: A topographic map: contour lines over slowly drifting hills, with heavier index lines and a light hillshade. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/contours.md
- `dither-fade`: A dithered edge that fades a section's content into a solid colour. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/dither-fade.md
- `dither-globe`: A rotating dithered globe with land, a lit terminator, and optional pulsing markers and arcs. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/dither-globe.md
- `dither-glow`: A soft dithered spotlight from an edge, a corner or any point, for heroes and cards. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/dither-glow.md
- `dither-gradient`: A linear, radial or conic gradient drawn as a dither, with a slow noise drift. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/dither-gradient.md
- `dither-orb`: A lit, dithered orb that slowly morphs and leans towards the pointer. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/dither-orb.md
- `dot-map`: A flat world map in dithered dots with pulsing markers, dithered halos and dotted arcs. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/dot-map.md
- `eclipse`: A dark disc with a glowing rim and a soft corona that breathes slowly. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/eclipse.md
- `fire`: Flames rising from the edge of the box, with a hot base, tapering tongues that lick up and tear off, and embers that drift above them. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/fire.md
- `flow-field`: A wind map: streamlines of a slowly turning, swirling flow, with bright streaks that travel along them and leave fading tails. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/flow-field.md
- `galaxy`: A tilted spiral galaxy turning slowly, with a bright core, arms with knots of stars, dust lanes and fixed stars behind. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/galaxy.md
- `halftone`: Print-style round dots on a rotated grid that grow with a noise, radial or linear source. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/halftone.md
- `horizon`: A planet's horizon from space: a lit rim, a drifting aurora glow and fixed stars. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/horizon.md
- `mesh-gradient`: Three to five colour blobs that drift and blend, drawn as a dither. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/mesh-gradient.md
- `metaballs`: Soft blobs that drift, merge and split like a lava lamp, as shaded shapes or rings of contour lines. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/metaballs.md
- `moire`: Two fine gratings of lines, rings or mesh laid over each other and sliding slowly, so huge interference bands bloom, sweep and turn across the box. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/moire.md
- `noise-field`: A slow, folding noise texture in four styles (smoke, ridges, contours, marble), with a sized mask that clears space for text. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/noise-field.md
- `plasma`: Classic plasma: overlapping sine waves that flow into each other, dithered in two colours or a palette. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/plasma.md
- `rain`: Rain on a window at night: soft out-of-focus city lights behind the glass, beads that show them brighter like tiny lenses, and bigger drops that slide down in jerky runs and leave wet trails. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/rain.md
- `retro-grid`: A perspective grid floor scrolling towards a horizon under a striped, glowing sun. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/retro-grid.md
- `ridgelines`: Stacked ridge lines like a pulsar plot, each hiding the ones behind it, with peaks that shift slowly. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/ridgelines.md
- `ripples`: Concentric rings spreading from one to four points and crossing like drops on still water. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/ripples.md
- `silk`: Folds of silk catching the light, with a bright highlight along each crest. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/silk.md
- `smoke`: Soft smoke billowing upward and thinning out, lit from above, with props for scale, height, wind and density. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/smoke.md
- `starfield`: Dithered stars in three parallax layers that twinkle and drift slowly. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/starfield.md
- `tunnel`: A slow flight down a tunnel of round or square rings, with spokes along the walls and fog at the vanishing point. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/tunnel.md
- `voronoi`: A cellular surface like soap foam, crackle glaze or raised stone tiles, with walls of one width and seeds that drift so cells swell, shrink and trade edges. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/voronoi.md
- `waves`: Layered swells under a glowing horizon, or thin lines like a sound wave. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/backgrounds/waves.md

## Charts

- `area-chart`: One or more series drawn as a crisp line over a dithered fill that is densest under the line. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/charts/area-chart.md
- `bar-chart`: Vertical bars, grouped or stacked, each filled with a dither and capped with a solid edge. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/charts/bar-chart.md
- `cartesian-chart`: The shared frame behind the area, line and bar charts: scales, axes, the hover readout, the legend and an accessible data table.
- `donut-chart`: A donut or pie chart drawn in dither cells, with a colour and texture per slice, a spotlight and a centre that follows the pointer. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/charts/donut-chart.md
- `gauge`: A radial gauge of dithered blocks that fill in to the value, with the reading in the middle. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/charts/gauge.md
- `heatmap`: A calendar or matrix heatmap built from dither cells: each square steps from a few dots to solid, with a readout and a level scale. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/charts/heatmap.md
- `line-chart`: Lines for one or more series, with optional dithered range bands and point markers. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/charts/line-chart.md
- `progress-bar`: A progress bar built from dither cells: any fill texture with a solid leading edge, stacked parts, step segments and an indeterminate comet. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/charts/progress-bar.md
- `radar-chart`: Series across several axes, drawn as polygons of dither cells whose density steps up ring by ring, with an axis scrub and legend spotlight. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/charts/radar-chart.md
- `sparkline`: A tiny inline trend for tables and stat cards: a line, a dithered area and a dot on the latest value. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/charts/sparkline.md
- `stat-card`: A KPI card with a value, a coloured delta and a dithered trend area on a dotted surface. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/charts/stat-card.md
- `uptime-bar`: A status-page row of daily dithered bars with per-day tooltips and overall uptime. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/charts/uptime-bar.md

## Interface

- `avatar`: A generative avatar drawn from a string as a mirrored dither face on a lit, dithered disc, with an overlapping avatar group. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/interface/avatar.md
- `dither-button`: A button with a lit, dithered surface that brightens on hover and presses in on click, in four fills, two variants and any palette colour. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/interface/dither-button.md
- `dither-card`: A card with a dithered glow in a corner or along an edge and a dithered rim on its border, which can grow on hover. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/interface/dither-card.md
- `dither-slider`: A range slider on Radix Slider whose fill is a Bayer ramp that gets denser towards a lit, dithered thumb, with one or two thumbs, steps, tick marks and a readout. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/interface/dither-slider.md
- `dither-switch`: A Radix toggle switch whose track fills with dither behind the thumb, stepping through the Bayer levels, with a lit dithered knob, four fills and any palette colour. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/interface/dither-switch.md
- `dither-tabs`: Tabs whose dithered pill or underline indicator glides to the chosen tab, dissolving out of the old one and in at the new one through the Bayer levels. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/interface/dither-tabs.md
- `divider`: A horizontal or vertical dithered rule with fading ends and an optional label. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/interface/divider.md
- `dropzone`: A file drop area with a dithered dashed border that marches round its edge, thickens and pulls a glow in on drag-over and turns red for a rejected file, with a file list showing dithered progress. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/interface/dropzone.md
- `empty-state`: A lit, dithered illustration (box, magnifier, folder or planet) with a title, a description and an action, for views with nothing in them yet. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/interface/empty-state.md
- `loader`: A small dithered loading indicator: a ring with a comet tail, three dissolving dots, a pulse or a bar. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/interface/loader.md
- `not-found`: A complete 404 block with a big dithered code, a message and actions. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/interface/not-found.md
- `skeleton`: Loading placeholders for blocks, text lines and avatars, drawn in dither, with a dense band that sweeps across or a pulse that steps through the Bayer levels. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/interface/skeleton.md

## Text

- `dissolve-text`: Text that dissolves in through Bayer thresholds by character, word or line, in any order, settling solid or into a dithered texture. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/text/dissolve-text.md
- `dither-number`: An animated number with tabular digits that roll or resolve through a dither, Intl formatting, prefix and suffix, colour and size presets. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/text/dither-number.md
- `dither-text`: Display text whose letters are filled with a dithered gradient, noise, dots or hatching in any palette colour, kept as real, selectable text. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/text/dither-text.md
- `scramble-text`: Text that resolves character by character through dithered blocks and glyphs, with no layout shift, on mount, in view, hover or text change. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/text/scramble-text.md

## Images

- `dither-image`: Any image dithered to a preset (ink, duotone, newsprint, gameboy, riso) or your own palette, resolving from coarse to fine. Docs: https://dithercn.dev/docs/images/dither-image.md

# Designing a landing page around a dither

A working dither on a generic page still reads as generated. The dither has to be the page's identity, drawn from what the product is, and the page around it has to be specific, quiet and true. Do this before you write a field.

## 1. Know the product

The page is for the product in this repo, not for dithercn. dithercn is the tool you build with: don't name it on the page, and don't make the page about dithering.

Read the README, `package.json`, the existing pages and any copy in the repo. Write yourself a short brief:

- What the product is and who it is for, in one sentence, in the product's own words.
- The one thing a visitor should do (install, sign up, download, book).
- The facts you can use: features, platforms, prices, numbers. Only facts that are in the repo or the user's message.

If there is no product to read about, ask the user what the page is for. If nobody can answer, pick something plausible, keep it modest, and say what you picked.

## 2. Find the dither in the subject

The hero dither should be something only this product would show. Take it from the product's own world and render that as a field, an image or a chart:

| The product is about             | A dither drawn from it                                                         |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Maps, outdoors, travel           | Contour lines of real-looking terrain, a route over them                       |
| Audio, music, voice              | A waveform or spectrum, ridgelines stacked like a spectrogram                  |
| Money, trading, analytics        | A price line or volume ridges, a dense band where activity is                  |
| Infrastructure, uptime, networks | Packets along paths, a grid of hosts, a pulse at the incident                  |
| Weather, climate, energy         | Isobars, a radar sweep, heat rising off a surface                              |
| Sleep, health, calm              | A slow breathing ring, a tide line, a night sky                                |
| Food, drink, physical goods      | The product photo itself through `ditherImage`, steam, grain, light on a table |
| Space, science, research         | An eclipse, a starfield, orbits, a particle trace                              |
| A developer tool or API          | The product's real output: its chart, its diagram, its data, dithered          |

A soft glow or noise field fits almost any product, which is why it says nothing about this one. Use one only as a supporting layer.

## 3. Compose the page

Spend the boldness in one place: the hero dither. Keep everything else quiet and disciplined.

**Pick the hero that fits**, not the split layout by default:

- **Full-bleed field.** The dither fills the hero and the headline sits on cleared ground (see [recipes.md](recipes.md#a-hero-that-clears-its-headline)).
- **The product shot.** A real product photo or screenshot, dithered with `ditherImage`, large, with the headline beside or above it.
- **One big number or object.** A glow, ring or gauge behind a real figure the product has, with the label in HTML.
- **A live demo.** The dither responds to one control (a slider, a toggle, a value), so the page shows what the product does.

**Build the rest from the content.** A section exists because the product has something to say there, not because landing pages have one.

- Show, don't list. One wide section that shows a feature working beats three cards that name three features.
- Vary the rhythm: a wide section, then a narrow one; text left, then right. Avoid rows of identical cards.
- Use at most two or three dithers on the page, each tied to content: the hero, a chart of real data, a dithered product photo, one section break.
- One accent colour at most, from the dither palette. The dither ink carries the page's colour; buttons and text stay in the theme.
- Typography carries the personality. One family is fine. Set a clear scale with weight and size, sentence case throughout.
- Keep vertical rhythm even (about `py-24` to `py-32` between sections on desktop, `py-16` on a phone) and line lengths under 80 characters.

## 4. Write true, plain copy

- The headline says what the product does for whom, in plain words. No wordplay that needs the subhead to explain it.
- The subhead adds two specifics: how it works, what you get.
- Buttons say what happens: "Download for Mac", "Start a free trial", "Read the docs".
- Use only facts from step 1. No invented stats, testimonials, customer logos, ratings or prices. If a section needs a number the product doesn't have, drop the section.

## 5. Don't ship the tells

These make a page read as generated, whatever the dither looks like:

- An all-caps, letter-spaced label above every heading, or monospace micro-labels used as decoration.
- Numbered markers (01, 02, 03) on things that aren't a sequence.
- One word in the headline set apart in italic, grey or colour; a serif display line followed by a grey second line.
- A row of three identical feature cards; a stats strip with invented numbers.
- Captions or pills laid over a visual ("Field study 01", "Signal / in motion"); a round arrow button on a card that goes nowhere.
- A fake product UI built from divs; fake testimonials; placeholder logos.
- A glowing orb or gradient in a rounded card as the whole hero.
- Em dashes, "elevate", "seamless", "unleash", "next-gen", an arrow on every link, decorative coloured dots.

## 6. Look at it as a visitor

Screenshot the whole page at 1440px and 390px, in light and dark mode. Go through every item in section 5 against the screenshots and the code, one by one, and fix each one you find; search the code for `—` and `uppercase`. Then answer honestly:

- In five seconds, can you tell what the product is and what to do next?
- Is the dither the first thing you notice, and does it belong to this product?
- Would this page be mistaken for any other product's page? If yes, the hero or the copy is generic: go back to step 2.
- Remove one element that isn't earning its place.

Then run every check in [quality.md](quality.md).

# Putting a dither on a page ## Layering A `DitherShader` fills its nearest positioned ancestor. Content goes in a sibling, above it: ```tsx
…
``` - `isolate` on the section keeps `-z-10` inside it, so the dither never slips behind the page background. - The section needs height from its content or a `min-h-*`. The shader takes the size it is given; zero height draws nothing. - Round corners and borders go on the section with `overflow-hidden`, so the canvas is clipped to them. - The shader ignores the pointer (`pointer-events-none`), so links and buttons above it stay clickable. ## Landing pages Read [landing-pages.md](landing-pages.md) first: it covers what the page is about and how it is composed. These are the placements. - **Hero:** a full-bleed background behind the headline. Clear the area under the text (tone 0 for lines and sparse patterns, 0.2 or less for soft fills) and let the dither peak towards the edges or a corner. Fade it out at the bottom with `smoothstep` on `uv.y` so the next section starts clean. - **Clearing space for text:** measure the text block and clear a rounded box around it, with the box passed to the field as a uniform. [recipes.md](recipes.md#a-hero-that-clears-its-headline) has the complete component. Measured this way the clearing fits the copy on a wide desktop and on a phone alike; an ellipse in `uv` is too big on one and too small on the other, and clips the corners of a text block. - **Section break:** a band 80 to 160px tall between sections, a dithered gradient from ink at one edge to paper at the other. - **Feature card:** a small shader or a `fillStyle("gradient")` layer behind a card's top half, under the icon and title. - **Dark plate:** a hero that is always dark wraps the section in `className="dark"` so `--dither-ink` and `--dither-paper` take the dark values there, whatever the site theme. - **Behind a big number or headline:** a glow centred on the text. Real text stays HTML on top; never draw text into the field. ## Dashboards - **Cards and tiles:** charts, meters and gauges are usually static SVG with `FillPattern`. They render on the server, cost nothing after paint and stay sharp. Use a shader in a card only for an ambient glow or a live status surface. - **Data first:** a meter or chart needs a readable label and value as HTML text, and an accessible name on the SVG (`role="img"` plus `aria-label` with the value, or `role="meter"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`). - **Track and fill:** draw the empty part of a meter or bar with a sparse fill (`level` 0.0625 to 0.125, or `fill="dotted"`) and the value with a dense one, so the empty track is still visible. - **Many on one page:** prefer SVG and CSS fills. At most 8 shaders hold a WebGL context at once. A shader scrolling onto the screen takes the context of one that has scrolled away; if more than 8 are on screen together, the extras show their fallback until one frees up. - **Colour meaning:** status colours from the palette (`"green"`, `"orange"`, `"red"`) map to good, warning and critical. Pair colour with a label or icon so it never carries meaning alone. ## Sizing cells `--dither-cell` sets the grain for the whole page (3px by default). Override it on a wrapper for one section (`style={{ "--dither-cell": "4px" }}`, typed as `React.CSSProperties & Record<"--dither-cell", string>`), or pass `cell` to one component. 2 to 3px reads as texture, 4 to 6px as a deliberate pixel look, 8px and up as pixel art. ## Next.js and server components - Files that use `DitherShader`, `useDitherColors`, `useFrameLoop` or a canvas start with `"use client"`. A server page imports and renders them like any component. - `FillPattern`, `DitherPattern`, `fillStyle`, `ditherMaskStyle`, `toCSS` and `toSVG` run on the server. - Inside a client component, generate SVG pattern ids with `useId()`. In a server component, derive them from a prop or a fixed name that is unique on the page.

# Quality checks

Run every check before calling a dither done. Each is something you can see or measure.

## Looks

- The dither pattern is visible: individual cells read at 100% zoom. A screenshot of flat colour means the tone sits at 0 or 1 everywhere; check the field's range.
- Shapes are round where they should be (aspect corrected) and lines keep one width across the box.
- Text over the dither has 4.5:1 contrast against the densest dots behind it.
- The box has the intended size at 1440px and 390px wide, with no horizontal scroll at 390px.
- Light and dark mode both look intentional, not one tuned and one washed out. Dark mode comes from the `.dark` class, not the media query, so toggle the class to check it (see theme.md).

## Motion and accessibility

- With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, the shader root has `data-state="static"` and shows a finished frame (`stillTime`). CSS transitions you add use `motion-safe:` or `motion-reduce:transition-none`. To check it, emulate the setting: `agent-browser set media dark reduced-motion`, Playwright `page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: "reduce" })`, or DevTools Rendering → prefers-reduced-motion.
- Decorative dithers are hidden from assistive tech. `DitherShader` sets `aria-hidden` by default; decorative SVGs get `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Data visuals have an accessible name with the value (`role="img"` and `aria-label="Storage: 72% used"`, or `role="meter"` with `aria-valuenow`), and the value is visible as text.
- Nothing flashes more than three times a second. Avoid per-frame random noise.

## Performance

- At most 8 `DitherShader`s are live at a time. For grids of thumbnails or many small pieces, use SVG or CSS fills.
- The `field` string is a module-level constant; options go through `uniforms`.
- Keep fields cheap: `fbm` is four noise calls. A field calling it a dozen times per cell, or with long loops, can drop frames on a phone. Sample a height function three times for contours, not thirty.
- Images are dithered at display size, one pixel per cell, never at full camera resolution.

## Console

- No `[dither-core] shader failed to compile` or `uniform … skipped` errors.
- No hydration warnings: client-only values (theme colours, sizes) are read in effects or hooks, not during render.

## Checking `data-state` in a browser

```js
[...document.querySelectorAll(".group\\/dither")].map((el) => el.dataset.state);
// "running" on screen, "static" under reduced motion, "paused" offscreen, "fallback" when nothing drew
```

# Palettes and theme

## The tokens

`dither-tokens` adds these CSS variables, with separate values under `:root` (light) and `.dark`:

| Variable                                                                        | Default               | Meaning                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `--dither-ink`                                                                  | `var(--primary)`      | The main dot colour, palette name `"ink"` |
| `--dither-paper`                                                                | `var(--background)`   | The colour behind the dots                |
| `--dither-cell`                                                                 | `3px`                 | One cell in CSS pixels                    |
| `--dither-bloom`                                                                | `1` dark, `0.6` light | Bloom strength                            |
| `--dither-color-blue`, `-purple`, `-green`, `-pink`, `-orange`, `-red`, `-grey` | tuned per theme       | The named colours                         |

Tailwind gets `dither-ink`, `dither-paper` and one utility per named colour (`bg-dither-green`, `text-dither-orange`).

## Choosing colours

- Use the names: `palette={["--dither-paper", "blue"]}`, `color="green"`. They are tuned to read on both black and white, so the dither follows light and dark with no extra work.
- Any CSS colour works where a `DitherColor` is accepted: `"--chart-2"`, `"var(--accent)"`, `"oklch(0.72 0.15 272)"`. Prefer variables; literal colours do not change with the theme.
- `"transparent"` as `palette[0]` lets whatever is behind the shader show through the paper cells. Use it when the dither sits on an image, a gradient or a card colour you don't control.
- Inside a card, set paper to the card colour so the dither blends: `palette={["--card", "ink"]}`, or set `--dither-paper: var(--card)` on the card.

## Palettes of more than two colours

The palette runs from tone 0 to tone 1, and each cell dithers between the two neighbouring colours:

```tsx
palette={["--dither-paper", "purple", "blue", "--dither-ink"]}
```

Order the colours by how strongly they stand out against the paper, from weakest to strongest, or the ramp jumps back and forth. A ramp is for colours that build in strength, like a glow from deep blue to white. A ramp of unrelated hues reads as noise, because neighbouring tones take unrelated colours. For many hues side by side, use the next section.

The field's tone snaps to `levels` steps before it is dithered, so a tone meant to be exactly one of the colours can land just beside it and pick up stray dots of its neighbour. Set `levels` so every stop is a step: `levels - 1` a multiple of `colours - 1`. Three colours: `levels={17}` (the bayer4 default already works). Four colours: `levels={13}` or `levels={19}`. Five colours: `levels={17}`.

## Any number of hues

The palette maps the field's tone to a colour, so in a palette of several hues the tone sets both the dot density and the colour. That suits ramps (a glow from deep blue to white), but it can't draw a red line and a blue line at the same strength, or a spectrum that runs along a line.

When the user asks for a rainbow, a spectrum, an RGB effect, or a different colour per line or shape, add a `colorField`: a second GLSL function that returns the dots' colour per cell, while `field` keeps deciding where the dots go. One shader, any colours, glows still dithered. See [fields.md](fields.md#colour) for the function, the `spectrum` and `paletteColor` helpers and building blocks, and [recipes.md](recipes.md#many-hues-a-spectrum-of-lines) for a complete component.

```tsx
<DitherShader
  field={FIELD} // where the dots go
  colorField={COLOR_FIELD} // what colour they are, e.g. return spectrum(uv.x);
  palette={["--background", "--foreground"]} // paper, then the colours paletteColor() reads
  className="absolute inset-0"
/>
```

Colour every shape in the scene from the one `colorField`: work out which shape a cell belongs to (a shared helper in the `field` string), then return that shape's colour, for example a hue that runs around a ring, a spectrum across a beam's thickness, and a hue along the lines. Don't run one shader per colour: each takes a WebGL context, and at most 8 run at once.

If the colour has to come from outside the shader (an image, a CSS gradient you already have, an animated SVG), the other way still works: put that layer under the shader and use `palette={["--background", "transparent"]}`, so tone 0 paints the background and tone 1 shows the layer. Give each shape its own layer positioned over it, a little larger than the shape and its glow.

A palette kept in a constant needs `as const`, because `palette` takes a tuple of at least two colours: `const PALETTE = ["#000", "transparent"] as const;`. Inline arrays work as they are.

## Light and dark

The tokens switch on a `.dark` class (shadcn's convention). Theme switches that change the class or style on `<html>` (next-themes and most others) make every shader re-read its colours and redraw. SVG and CSS fills use `var()` and follow instantly.

If the app has no theme switcher, nothing adds `.dark`, so the dark values never apply, even when the operating system is in dark mode. Look for `next-themes` or a `dark` class in the root layout. Without one, ask before adding next-themes (`<ThemeProvider attribute="class" defaultTheme="system" enableSystem>` around the body, `suppressHydrationWarning` on `<html>`); to test dark mode meanwhile, add the class by hand in the browser: `document.documentElement.classList.add("dark")`.

Check both themes. Common fixes:

- Ink too heavy in light mode: lower the peak tone, or use a lighter named colour.
- Glow invisible in light mode: light paper needs a darker ink. `"ink"` and the named colours already flip; literal colours don't.
- A section that is always dark: `className="dark"` on its wrapper.

## Retinting a section

Variables cascade. Set them on a wrapper to retint everything inside:

```tsx
<section style={{ "--dither-ink": "var(--chart-2)" } as React.CSSProperties}>
  …
</section>
```

## Contrast

Ink and paper need a clear difference for the pattern to read. For anything that carries information (charts, meters, status), aim for about 4.5:1 between them. Quiet backgrounds can go lower; text placed over a dither still needs 4.5:1 against the densest dots behind it.

# dithercn

dithercn is a dither engine. `dither-core` (installed into `lib/dither`) turns a tone you compute into ordered dither dots, in your theme's colours, with motion, resizing and reduced motion handled. You build the dither the user asked for on top of it. The dithercn components are examples of what the engine can do, not a menu to pick from. Install one only when it is exactly what the user asked for. Otherwise write your own, and borrow technique from the closest example's source.

## 1. Set up the engine

Find the engine: `lib/dither/index.ts`, under the `lib` alias in `components.json` (imports below use `@/lib/dither`; use the project's alias). If it is missing, install it from the dithercn registry:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add https://dithercn.dev/r/dither-core.json
```

If it exists, check that it is current: `grep -q colorField lib/dither/shader.tsx` (with the project's path). An engine installed before `colorField` existed lacks it and the `spectrum` and `paletteColor` helpers, and TypeScript reports `Property 'colorField' does not exist`. Replace the engine's files; this keeps the project's `lib/utils.ts` (`yes n` answers no to every question about overwriting a file) and restores `lib/dither/export.ts`:

```bash
rm -rf lib/dither && yes n | npx shadcn@latest add https://dithercn.dev/r/dither-core.json https://dithercn.dev/r/dither-export.json
```

Don't use `--overwrite`: it also replaces `lib/utils.ts`. If the project edited files inside `lib/dither`, tell the user before replacing them.

That also installs `dither-tokens`: the CSS variables `--dither-ink`, `--dither-paper`, `--dither-cell`, `--dither-bloom` and `--dither-color-<name>`, written into the project's global CSS and mapped to the shadcn `--primary` and `--background`. The engine needs React 19 and Tailwind CSS v4.

Done when `lib/dither/index.ts` exists, `lib/dither/shader.tsx` mentions `colorField`, and the global CSS defines `--dither-ink`.

## 3. Build it

If the dither is for a landing page, or a section of one, read [landing-pages.md](references/landing-pages.md) before anything else. A good dither on a generic page still looks generated: the page has to be about the product, and the dither has to come from it.

1. Read the reference named for your technique, and [recipes.md](references/recipes.md) for complete, working components to adapt.
2. Write the component in its own file. `"use client"` when it uses `DitherShader`, hooks or a canvas; `FillPattern`, `DitherPattern`, `fillStyle` and `ditherMaskStyle` render on the server.
3. Give it typed props for what the user would tweak (colour, intensity, speed, scale, value), with defaults that already look good.
4. Place it with [placement.md](references/placement.md): a shader fills a positioned parent (`absolute inset-0`), and content sits in a sibling above it.
5. Colour it with [theme.md](references/theme.md): palette names such as `"ink"` and `"blue"`, or CSS variables, so it follows light and dark.

Done when the component renders the requested look with no `[dither-core]` errors in the console.

## 4. Check it in a browser

Open the page and look at it. Screenshot it if you can, at desktop and phone widths, in light and dark mode, and once with reduced motion (`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`). Hold it to [quality.md](references/quality.md).

Done when every check in quality.md passes. A screenshot that shows flat colour, a solid block or an empty box means the field returns the wrong range or the parent has no size: fix it and look again.

## Rules for every dither

- A field returns a continuous tone in [0, 1]: 0 paper, 1 ink. The engine quantises and dithers it, so write smooth math (`smoothstep`, `exp`, `mix`) and leave thresholds and Bayer matrices to the engine.
- `uv` runs 0 to 1 on both axes with y up. Multiply x by `res.x / res.y` before measuring distances, or circles stretch into ovals.
- Paint with theme colours (`"ink"`, palette names, `--css-variables`). Literal colours, and `spectrum()` in a `colorField`, are for when the user asks for specific colours or a rainbow.
- Text sits on clear ground. Fade the tone down where text goes: to 0 for lines and sparse patterns, to 0.2 or less for soft fills. Text contrast stays at 4.5:1 or better.
- Motion is slow, a drift of a few percent of the box per second. Choose `stillTime` so the reduced-motion frame looks finished.

# dither-core API Everything imports from `@/lib/dither` (the project's `lib` alias), except export functions, which live in `@/lib/dither/export`. The installed source in `lib/dither/` is the final word; each export has a doc comment. ## Shared types ```ts type DitherColor = DitherColorName | string; // A palette name ("ink" | "blue" | "purple" | "green" | "pink" | "orange" | "red" | "grey"), // a CSS variable name ("--chart-1"), or any CSS colour ("var(--chart-1)", "oklch(0.7 0.15 272)", "#fff", "transparent"). // Names win over CSS keywords: "red" is the dithercn red. type DitherPalette = readonly [DitherColor, DitherColor, ...DitherColor[]]; // From tone 0 (paper) to tone 1 (ink). At least two. type DitherMatrix = "bayer2" | "bayer4" | "bayer8" | "blue-noise"; ``` Matrices: `bayer4` is the default, a regular printed crosshatch with 17 tones. `bayer8` has 65 tones and finer gradients. `bayer2` is chunky, 5 tones. `blue-noise` is a 64×64 tile with no visible grid, like film grain; best for large soft surfaces. `level` (static fills) and tone (shaders) both mean coverage from 0 (no cells inked) to 1 (all). With `bayer4`, `k / 16` inks exactly k of every 16 cells. ## DitherShader A client component that draws a GLSL field as a dither on a WebGL canvas at one canvas pixel per cell, scaled up with crisp edges. ```tsx } className="absolute inset-0" // plus any div prop: style, ref, id, data-* /> ``` - The root is `relative overflow-hidden pointer-events-none`, `aria-hidden` by default. It renders no children: put content in a sibling. - It sizes to its box. A box with no height draws nothing. - `fallback` shows before the first frame, without WebGL, and while the shader is far offscreen. Default: flat `palette[0]`. Make it resemble the dither (a CSS gradient in the ink colour). - Free behaviour: resize observer, whole-device-pixel cells, theme changes re-read the palette, pauses offscreen and in hidden tabs, a still frame under reduced motion, context loss recovery. At most 8 shaders hold a WebGL context at once (`MAX_LIVE_CONTEXTS`); past that, a shader coming on screen takes one from a shader just off screen, never from one still on screen, and waits otherwise, showing `fallback`. - `data-state` on the root: `running`, `paused` (offscreen or hidden tab), `static` (reduced motion or `animate={false}`), `fallback` (no frame drawn). - With `colorField`, each cell is either paper (`palette[0]`) or the colour `colorField` returns there; the field's tone still decides which, so density and colour are independent. The rest of the palette is what the `paletteColor(x)` helper reads. Without it, the palette maps tone to colour as before. - Changing `uniforms`, `palette`, `matrix`, `levels` or `speed` is cheap. Changing the `field` or `colorField` string recompiles, so keep it a module constant and drive variation through uniforms. - `DitherShaderProps` is exported. # Designing a landing page around a dither

A working dither on a generic page still reads as generated. The dither has to be the page's identity, drawn from what the product is, and the page around it has to be specific, quiet and true. Do this before you write a field.

## 1. Know the product

The page is for the product in this repo, not for dithercn. dithercn is the tool you build with: don't name it on the page, and don't make the page about dithering.

Read the README, `package.json`, the existing pages and any copy in the repo. Write yourself a short brief:

- What the product is and who it is for, in one sentence, in the product's own words.
- The one thing a visitor should do (install, sign up, download, book).
- The facts you can use: features, platforms, prices, numbers. Only facts that are in the repo or the user's message.

If there is no product to read about, ask the user what the page is for. If nobody can answer, pick something plausible, keep it modest, and say what you picked.

## 2. Find the dither in the subject

The hero dither should be something only this product would show. Take it from the product's own world and render that as a field, an image or a chart:

| The product is about             | A dither drawn from it                                                         |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Maps, outdoors, travel           | Contour lines of real-looking terrain, a route over them                       |
| Audio, music, voice              | A waveform or spectrum, ridgelines stacked like a spectrogram                  |
| Money, trading, analytics        | A price line or volume ridges, a dense band where activity is                  |
| Infrastructure, uptime, networks | Packets along paths, a grid of hosts, a pulse at the incident                  |
| Weather, climate, energy         | Isobars, a radar sweep, heat rising off a surface                              |
| Sleep, health, calm              | A slow breathing ring, a tide line, a night sky                                |
| Food, drink, physical goods      | The product photo itself through `ditherImage`, steam, grain, light on a table |
| Space, science, research         | An eclipse, a starfield, orbits, a particle trace                              |
| A developer tool or API          | The product's real output: its chart, its diagram, its data, dithered          |

A soft glow or noise field fits almost any product, which is why it says nothing about this one. Use one only as a supporting layer.

## 3. Compose the page

Spend the boldness in one place: the hero dither. Keep everything else quiet and disciplined.

**Pick the hero that fits**, not the split layout by default:

- **Full-bleed field.** The dither fills the hero and the headline sits on cleared ground (see [recipes.md](recipes.md#a-hero-that-clears-its-headline)).
- **The product shot.** A real product photo or screenshot, dithered with `ditherImage`, large, with the headline beside or above it.
- **One big number or object.** A glow, ring or gauge behind a real figure the product has, with the label in HTML.
- **A live demo.** The dither responds to one control (a slider, a toggle, a value), so the page shows what the product does.

**Build the rest from the content.** A section exists because the product has something to say there, not because landing pages have one.

- Show, don't list. One wide section that shows a feature working beats three cards that name three features.
- Vary the rhythm: a wide section, then a narrow one; text left, then right. Avoid rows of identical cards.
- Use at most two or three dithers on the page, each tied to content: the hero, a chart of real data, a dithered product photo, one section break.
- One accent colour at most, from the dither palette. The dither ink carries the page's colour; buttons and text stay in the theme.
- Typography carries the personality. One family is fine. Set a clear scale with weight and size, sentence case throughout.
- Keep vertical rhythm even (about `py-24` to `py-32` between sections on desktop, `py-16` on a phone) and line lengths under 80 characters.

## 4. Write true, plain copy

- The headline says what the product does for whom, in plain words. No wordplay that needs the subhead to explain it.
- The subhead adds two specifics: how it works, what you get.
- Buttons say what happens: "Download for Mac", "Start a free trial", "Read the docs".
- Use only facts from step 1. No invented stats, testimonials, customer logos, ratings or prices. If a section needs a number the product doesn't have, drop the section.

## 5. Don't ship the tells

These make a page read as generated, whatever the dither looks like:

- An all-caps, letter-spaced label above every heading, or monospace micro-labels used as decoration.
- Numbered markers (01, 02, 03) on things that aren't a sequence.
- One word in the headline set apart in italic, grey or colour; a serif display line followed by a grey second line.
- A row of three identical feature cards; a stats strip with invented numbers.
- Captions or pills laid over a visual ("Field study 01", "Signal / in motion"); a round arrow button on a card that goes nowhere.
- A fake product UI built from divs; fake testimonials; placeholder logos.
- A glowing orb or gradient in a rounded card as the whole hero.
- Em dashes, "elevate", "seamless", "unleash", "next-gen", an arrow on every link, decorative coloured dots.

## 6. Look at it as a visitor

Screenshot the whole page at 1440px and 390px, in light and dark mode. Go through every item in section 5 against the screenshots and the code, one by one, and fix each one you find; search the code for `—` and `uppercase`. Then answer honestly:

- In five seconds, can you tell what the product is and what to do next?
- Is the dither the first thing you notice, and does it belong to this product?
- Would this page be mistaken for any other product's page? If yes, the hero or the copy is generic: go back to step 2.
- Remove one element that isn't earning its place.

Then run every check in [quality.md](quality.md).

# Putting a dither on a page ## Layering A `DitherShader` fills its nearest positioned ancestor. Content goes in a sibling, above it: ```tsx
…
``` - `isolate` on the section keeps `-z-10` inside it, so the dither never slips behind the page background. - The section needs height from its content or a `min-h-*`. The shader takes the size it is given; zero height draws nothing. - Round corners and borders go on the section with `overflow-hidden`, so the canvas is clipped to them. - The shader ignores the pointer (`pointer-events-none`), so links and buttons above it stay clickable. ## Landing pages Read [landing-pages.md](landing-pages.md) first: it covers what the page is about and how it is composed. These are the placements. - **Hero:** a full-bleed background behind the headline. Clear the area under the text (tone 0 for lines and sparse patterns, 0.2 or less for soft fills) and let the dither peak towards the edges or a corner. Fade it out at the bottom with `smoothstep` on `uv.y` so the next section starts clean. - **Clearing space for text:** measure the text block and clear a rounded box around it, with the box passed to the field as a uniform. [recipes.md](recipes.md#a-hero-that-clears-its-headline) has the complete component. Measured this way the clearing fits the copy on a wide desktop and on a phone alike; an ellipse in `uv` is too big on one and too small on the other, and clips the corners of a text block. - **Section break:** a band 80 to 160px tall between sections, a dithered gradient from ink at one edge to paper at the other. - **Feature card:** a small shader or a `fillStyle("gradient")` layer behind a card's top half, under the icon and title. - **Dark plate:** a hero that is always dark wraps the section in `className="dark"` so `--dither-ink` and `--dither-paper` take the dark values there, whatever the site theme. - **Behind a big number or headline:** a glow centred on the text. Real text stays HTML on top; never draw text into the field. ## Dashboards - **Cards and tiles:** charts, meters and gauges are usually static SVG with `FillPattern`. They render on the server, cost nothing after paint and stay sharp. Use a shader in a card only for an ambient glow or a live status surface. - **Data first:** a meter or chart needs a readable label and value as HTML text, and an accessible name on the SVG (`role="img"` plus `aria-label` with the value, or `role="meter"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`). - **Track and fill:** draw the empty part of a meter or bar with a sparse fill (`level` 0.0625 to 0.125, or `fill="dotted"`) and the value with a dense one, so the empty track is still visible. - **Many on one page:** prefer SVG and CSS fills. At most 8 shaders hold a WebGL context at once. A shader scrolling onto the screen takes the context of one that has scrolled away; if more than 8 are on screen together, the extras show their fallback until one frees up. - **Colour meaning:** status colours from the palette (`"green"`, `"orange"`, `"red"`) map to good, warning and critical. Pair colour with a label or icon so it never carries meaning alone. ## Sizing cells `--dither-cell` sets the grain for the whole page (3px by default). Override it on a wrapper for one section (`style={{ "--dither-cell": "4px" }}`, typed as `React.CSSProperties & Record<"--dither-cell", string>`), or pass `cell` to one component. 2 to 3px reads as texture, 4 to 6px as a deliberate pixel look, 8px and up as pixel art. ## Next.js and server components - Files that use `DitherShader`, `useDitherColors`, `useFrameLoop` or a canvas start with `"use client"`. A server page imports and renders them like any component. - `FillPattern`, `DitherPattern`, `fillStyle`, `ditherMaskStyle`, `toCSS` and `toSVG` run on the server. - Inside a client component, generate SVG pattern ids with `useId()`. In a server component, derive them from a prop or a fixed name that is unique on the page.

# Quality checks

Run every check before calling a dither done. Each is something you can see or measure.

## Looks

- The dither pattern is visible: individual cells read at 100% zoom. A screenshot of flat colour means the tone sits at 0 or 1 everywhere; check the field's range.
- Shapes are round where they should be (aspect corrected) and lines keep one width across the box.
- Text over the dither has 4.5:1 contrast against the densest dots behind it.
- The box has the intended size at 1440px and 390px wide, with no horizontal scroll at 390px.
- Light and dark mode both look intentional, not one tuned and one washed out. Dark mode comes from the `.dark` class, not the media query, so toggle the class to check it (see theme.md).

## Motion and accessibility

- With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, the shader root has `data-state="static"` and shows a finished frame (`stillTime`). CSS transitions you add use `motion-safe:` or `motion-reduce:transition-none`. To check it, emulate the setting: `agent-browser set media dark reduced-motion`, Playwright `page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: "reduce" })`, or DevTools Rendering → prefers-reduced-motion.
- Decorative dithers are hidden from assistive tech. `DitherShader` sets `aria-hidden` by default; decorative SVGs get `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Data visuals have an accessible name with the value (`role="img"` and `aria-label="Storage: 72% used"`, or `role="meter"` with `aria-valuenow`), and the value is visible as text.
- Nothing flashes more than three times a second. Avoid per-frame random noise.

## Performance

- At most 8 `DitherShader`s are live at a time. For grids of thumbnails or many small pieces, use SVG or CSS fills.
- The `field` string is a module-level constant; options go through `uniforms`.
- Keep fields cheap: `fbm` is four noise calls. A field calling it a dozen times per cell, or with long loops, can drop frames on a phone. Sample a height function three times for contours, not thirty.
- Images are dithered at display size, one pixel per cell, never at full camera resolution.

## Console

- No `[dither-core] shader failed to compile` or `uniform … skipped` errors.
- No hydration warnings: client-only values (theme colours, sizes) are read in effects or hooks, not during render.

## Checking `data-state` in a browser

```js
[...document.querySelectorAll(".group\\/dither")].map((el) => el.dataset.state);
// "running" on screen, "static" under reduced motion, "paused" offscreen, "fallback" when nothing drew
```

# Palettes and theme

## The tokens

`dither-tokens` adds these CSS variables, with separate values under `:root` (light) and `.dark`:

| Variable                                                                        | Default               | Meaning                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `--dither-ink`                                                                  | `var(--primary)`      | The main dot colour, palette name `"ink"` |
| `--dither-paper`                                                                | `var(--background)`   | The colour behind the dots                |
| `--dither-cell`                                                                 | `3px`                 | One cell in CSS pixels                    |
| `--dither-bloom`                                                                | `1` dark, `0.6` light | Bloom strength                            |
| `--dither-color-blue`, `-purple`, `-green`, `-pink`, `-orange`, `-red`, `-grey` | tuned per theme       | The named colours                         |

Tailwind gets `dither-ink`, `dither-paper` and one utility per named colour (`bg-dither-green`, `text-dither-orange`).

## Choosing colours

- Use the names: `palette={["--dither-paper", "blue"]}`, `color="green"`. They are tuned to read on both black and white, so the dither follows light and dark with no extra work.
- Any CSS colour works where a `DitherColor` is accepted: `"--chart-2"`, `"var(--accent)"`, `"oklch(0.72 0.15 272)"`. Prefer variables; literal colours do not change with the theme.
- `"transparent"` as `palette[0]` lets whatever is behind the shader show through the paper cells. Use it when the dither sits on an image, a gradient or a card colour you don't control.
- Inside a card, set paper to the card colour so the dither blends: `palette={["--card", "ink"]}`, or set `--dither-paper: var(--card)` on the card.

## Palettes of more than two colours

The palette runs from tone 0 to tone 1, and each cell dithers between the two neighbouring colours:

```tsx
palette={["--dither-paper", "purple", "blue", "--dither-ink"]}
```

Order the colours by how strongly they stand out against the paper, from weakest to strongest, or the ramp jumps back and forth. A ramp is for colours that build in strength, like a glow from deep blue to white. A ramp of unrelated hues reads as noise, because neighbouring tones take unrelated colours. For many hues side by side, use the next section.

The field's tone snaps to `levels` steps before it is dithered, so a tone meant to be exactly one of the colours can land just beside it and pick up stray dots of its neighbour. Set `levels` so every stop is a step: `levels - 1` a multiple of `colours - 1`. Three colours: `levels={17}` (the bayer4 default already works). Four colours: `levels={13}` or `levels={19}`. Five colours: `levels={17}`.

## Any number of hues

The palette maps the field's tone to a colour, so in a palette of several hues the tone sets both the dot density and the colour. That suits ramps (a glow from deep blue to white), but it can't draw a red line and a blue line at the same strength, or a spectrum that runs along a line.

When the user asks for a rainbow, a spectrum, an RGB effect, or a different colour per line or shape, add a `colorField`: a second GLSL function that returns the dots' colour per cell, while `field` keeps deciding where the dots go. One shader, any colours, glows still dithered. See [fields.md](fields.md#colour) for the function, the `spectrum` and `paletteColor` helpers and building blocks, and [recipes.md](recipes.md#many-hues-a-spectrum-of-lines) for a complete component.

```tsx
<DitherShader
  field={FIELD} // where the dots go
  colorField={COLOR_FIELD} // what colour they are, e.g. return spectrum(uv.x);
  palette={["--background", "--foreground"]} // paper, then the colours paletteColor() reads
  className="absolute inset-0"
/>
```

Colour every shape in the scene from the one `colorField`: work out which shape a cell belongs to (a shared helper in the `field` string), then return that shape's colour, for example a hue that runs around a ring, a spectrum across a beam's thickness, and a hue along the lines. Don't run one shader per colour: each takes a WebGL context, and at most 8 run at once.

If the colour has to come from outside the shader (an image, a CSS gradient you already have, an animated SVG), the other way still works: put that layer under the shader and use `palette={["--background", "transparent"]}`, so tone 0 paints the background and tone 1 shows the layer. Give each shape its own layer positioned over it, a little larger than the shape and its glow.

A palette kept in a constant needs `as const`, because `palette` takes a tuple of at least two colours: `const PALETTE = ["#000", "transparent"] as const;`. Inline arrays work as they are.

## Light and dark

The tokens switch on a `.dark` class (shadcn's convention). Theme switches that change the class or style on `<html>` (next-themes and most others) make every shader re-read its colours and redraw. SVG and CSS fills use `var()` and follow instantly.

If the app has no theme switcher, nothing adds `.dark`, so the dark values never apply, even when the operating system is in dark mode. Look for `next-themes` or a `dark` class in the root layout. Without one, ask before adding next-themes (`<ThemeProvider attribute="class" defaultTheme="system" enableSystem>` around the body, `suppressHydrationWarning` on `<html>`); to test dark mode meanwhile, add the class by hand in the browser: `document.documentElement.classList.add("dark")`.

Check both themes. Common fixes:

- Ink too heavy in light mode: lower the peak tone, or use a lighter named colour.
- Glow invisible in light mode: light paper needs a darker ink. `"ink"` and the named colours already flip; literal colours don't.
- A section that is always dark: `className="dark"` on its wrapper.

## Retinting a section

Variables cascade. Set them on a wrapper to retint everything inside:

```tsx
<section style={{ "--dither-ink": "var(--chart-2)" } as React.CSSProperties}>
  …
</section>
```

## Contrast

Ink and paper need a clear difference for the pattern to read. For anything that carries information (charts, meters, status), aim for about 4.5:1 between them. Quiet backgrounds can go lower; text placed over a dither still needs 4.5:1 against the densest dots behind it.
